claim: For every integer \(N\ge4\), there are two coarsening filtrations of finite topologies on the same \(N\)-point set whose uniform normalized minimal-open discrepancy is \(1/N^2\), while the degree-one bottleneck distance of the induced persistence diagrams is exactly \(1\). Consequently, no constant \(C\) independent of \(N\) can bound \(d_B\le C\Delta_N\) for all such filtrations.

correctness.rationale: The two middle-stage order complexes are explicit: a four-cycle with integral \(H_1\) equal to \(\mathbb Z\), and a disk formed by two triangles sharing an edge. The discrete-to-middle-to-indiscrete coarsening filtration gives exactly the interval \((0,2)\) in degree one for the first family and no degree-one interval for the second. Only one minimal open changes by one point, so the normalized discrepancy is exactly \(1/N^2\); the bottleneck cost to the diagonal is exactly \(1\).

value.rationale: The result gives an exact quantitative obstruction to treating normalized minimal-open discrepancy as a dimension-independent stability metric for persistence: one altered comparability destroys a degree-one interval of fixed lifetime while the normalized discrepancy decays quadratically with the number of points. This separates empirical correlations from universal stability claims and identifies the need for additional structural hypotheses.
